newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market dormant- private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market dormant- private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were dormant, with no reported trades, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were scattered at $64.00 to $65.00 per cwt, but cattle owners passed on the bids and held out for $67.00, the sources said.

Forecasts for below normal temperatures this week in the Plains and below-zero (Fahrenheit) readings by the weekend with wind chill factors of 20 to 30 below zero spurred ideas that packers would pay steady to higher for quick shipments, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma showlists were estimated to total near 70,000 head, up about 6,000 from last week and Kansas showlists were pegged near 87,000 head, up 10,500, sources said.
Showlists this week were larger than last because of carryover of light-weight cattle, cattle feeders said. The lighter weights reflected feedlots' current marketing status.

A snowstorm moving into the southern Panhandle overnight was not expected to have much impact on major feedlots unless it shifts northward. The current expected path put the storm's heaviest snow through Lubbock and Midland, forecasters said.
